cells.tense: Right now you can see how much you can give and you are giving it.
cells.ask: Offer one person something concrete — an hour, a hand, a name that opens a door — sized so you can do it again next week.
cells.core:
There's a measure in what you hand over. You give where there's a need and you stop where giving more would cost you the strength that makes giving possible. That stopping is part of it, not a failure of it.

Out here the picture isn't whole, and you're not waiting for it to be. One step is visible and you take it, then the next one shows up. That's how you move through the unlit part. The measure is what keeps what you offer from becoming a drain — give past it and the thing changes character, and the people receiving it can feel the change even when you can't. Where the line sits is yours to say. Keeping it is the practice.
cells.sheetLine: You know how much to give, and you give it.
cells.verb: sharing your strength by measure, where it is needed
cells.place: in the half-light, where one step is visible and the rest is not

cells.tense: You are bracing for a need that has not arrived yet and may never arrive.
cells.ask: Leave one person's problem alone for a week. When it stays unsolved, notice it did not become yours.
cells.core:
You're making the move before the need shows up. You're reading ahead in a situation where the next page isn't written, and the picture you get is one where something falls apart if you don't get there first — so your strength goes out ahead of you, before anyone has asked.

The half-light is what sets this off, and it's also the condition you're built to move through. The difference is that you're not moving through it, you're bracing in it, trying to get to certainty before the situation has offered any. What you give arrives already decided for the person receiving it, and a hand that arrives decided is hard to take. The steady part can stay; the pushing ahead is what to set down.

cells.tense: There was a moment when what you offered was not taken, and you are still standing in it.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you need from them this week. State it plainly and let them answer however they answer.
cells.core:
You've kept your strength in. When something comes up and you have what it would take to help, you don't hand it over, and you don't ask for anything either. What's gone quiet is the offering, not the strength.

The ground is dim around you too. When someone asks what you want or what's next, you don't put a direction out, and a direction is what lights the next step. That's the part sitting still. A small ask, to one person, said plainly, is enough to find out whether the door is still shut. It usually isn't, and you'll know either way.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped putting it out. The strength is still there.

cells.tense: The directions you are steering by are already being chosen by something you do not name.
cells.ask: Write the one thing you are aiming for in the next month on a piece of paper and pin it where you will see it.
cells.core:
You're already pointing somewhere. There's a direction running under the week — what you say yes to, what you quietly drop, what you keep in the room. But when you talk about it, it turns into the situation deciding, or the timing, or other people needing you. The aiming is happening. Saying so isn't.

You can hold your strength out in the open and still not know which light you're facing while you do it. That's the part running unclaimed. Putting the aim into words doesn't change what you do with the strength; it just means you're the one who chose where it goes. That's a smaller thing than it sounds, and it changes who is carrying the decision.

attempts.check: Unsupported: I read 'offered' as one thing running the other way — the person waiting for a decision to be made for them, or for an ask to come first — when the record shows nothing about who offered what; it only says resources flow where needed and the seat navigates ambiguity. A reader could say the obstacle is resources or another person, not their own held-off move, and the cell would be wrong about them and still usable only if the ask stands on its own. It does: telling one person what you need and letting them answer is useful whether or not my read was right, since either way the person gets information they didn't have, and nothing in it waits on the response. Sentence that serves me more than them: 'You're waiting for it to be decided' — that one flatters the read and skips what I don't know. Fixing before writing: each core keeps the mechanism as one person's next move in a moment they'd recognise, no claims about why, and the ask never makes usefulness conditional on the read being true.

attempts.check: Unsupported: I read the Too Much cell as a person bracing against a future need that hasn't arrived, when the record only says the capacity in excess crosses the map toward obsessive calculation of fairness. A reader could say the problem is that they are giving too little, not too much, and the cell would be wrong about them and still useful only if the ask can stand alone. It can: leaving one person's problem alone for a week teaches something about where the line sits whether or not the read was right, and nothing in it waits on my being correct. Sentence that serves me more than them: 'There's a future in your head where everyone falls apart without you' — that one invents a scene and a population to make the read feel true. Fixing before writing: each core keeps to one capacity in one kind of moment, no certification of what the person knows, no cause assigned to the Too Little standing-place, no universals, and the ask never makes its usefulness conditional on the read being true.
